children: Manufacturing orders in Germany climbed again in July, continuing to defy the impact of surging energy prices as the conflict in the Middle East persists.

Factory orders in the eurozone's largest economy rose 2.5% on month, following an upwardly revised 3.7% rise in June, data agency Destatis said Friday. A consensus of economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal had expected a small fall of 0.1%.

That marked a third consecutive monthly increase, continuing a decent run of industrial data even as the war in Iran sent oil-and-gas prices higher. Industrial-production data for July is due on Monday, having also risen for the prior three-straight months.
Almost all of July's rise in orders was down to larger orders of transport equipment, a grouping of goods that includes aircraft, ships, trains and military vehicles, Destatis said.
However, stockpiling could still be propelling that upturn as supply constraints continued with the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Some of the increase in July was driven by a 4.3% jump in intermediate goods orders--those used to make other products like chemicals or semiconductors. Since consumer products orders declined 4.8%, it suggests those intermediate goods aren't being immediately turned into final products.

title: German Factory Orders Climb for Third Straight Month
